name: ComoRAG

paper.title: ComoRAG: A Cognitive-Inspired Memory-Organized RAG for Stateful Long Narrative Reasoning

construction.unit: three indexes over a book (raw chunks with KG triples, cluster summaries, window summaries) + per-question memory units (probe, evidence, cue)
construction.kept_as: verbatim 512-token chunks plus LLM summaries; memory units hold LLM-written cues
construction.processing: LLM extracts triples per chunk (HippoRAG 2 recipe); GMM clusters summarized recursively (RAPTOR recipe); non-overlapping windows of W chunks summarized in story order

organization.structure: Veridical layer (chunk-entity graph), Semantic layer (summary tree), Episodic layer (timeline summaries); a per-question memory pool beside them
organization.stores: three BGE-M3 embedding stores + igraph KG; memory pool of units (probe, evidence, cue, embedding)
organization.index: BGE-M3 dense vectors; fact embeddings seed Personalized PageRank on the KG

management.operations: knowledge source is static; each failed cycle appends new memory units and one fused note to the per-question pool
management.forgetting: pool is discarded after each question

retrieval.query: question at step 0; afterwards up to 3 LLM-written probes per cycle
retrieval.candidates: Veridical: top-5 facts by similarity, LLM fact filter, PPR over KG; Semantic and Episodic: dense similarity; top 50 per layer, items already in the pool dropped
retrieval.selection: per-layer token budget; Mem-Fuse picks the top 50% of pool units by similarity to the question
retrieval.budget: answer context capped at 6k tokens, 8:2:2:1 across Veridical, Semantic, Episodic and fused history (paper); code caps each layer separately (3,000/1,000/1,000 default, 2,000 each in the example script)

use.context: step 0: raw retrieved chunks and summaries; later cycles: LLM cues of the new units plus fused notes
use.reasoning: answer LLM returns an answer or a failure signal ('*'); on failure another probe cycle runs, up to 5 cycles

classify.note: Three different indexes, of which the Veridical one (PPR over a KG) carries most of the gain in the ablation; Semantic and Episodic use plain dense search. The set is fixed by top-50 plus a token cap; the LLM only decides whether to run another probe cycle and what to probe.

stages.ingestion: The book is split into 512-token chunks.
stages.construction: Three indexes are built once: chunks with LLM-extracted triples linked into an entity graph (Veridical), recursive GMM-cluster summaries (Semantic), and summaries of consecutive chunk windows in story order (Episodic).
stages.organization: The three layers are separate embedding stores (BGE-M3); a question-specific memory pool holds units of (probe, retrieved evidence from one layer, LLM cue).
stages.update: When the answer LLM signals failure, new units from the probes are appended to the pool and an LLM fuses the most question-similar half of the pool into a background note.
stages.retrieval: Each query hits all three layers (PPR over the KG for Veridical, dense search for the others), keeps the top 50 per layer minus items already seen, then cuts to a per-layer token budget; after a failure an LLM writes up to 3 new probes that are searched the same way.
stages.answer: Step 0 answers from the raw evidence; later cycles answer from the new cues plus fused notes, with multiple-choice options shown only at this step.

summary: Long-narrative RAG that, when a first answer fails, loops up to five times: an LLM writes new probes, evidence from three indexes (entity graph, summary tree, timeline summaries) is turned into query-focused cues, and past cues are fused before answering again.
notes: Venue checked: AAAI 2026, Proceedings vol. 40 no. 39, 'AAAI Technical Track on Natural Language Processing IV', pp. 33557-33565 (ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/40644); the repo README calls it a poster. Paper text from arXiv v3 (12 Nov 2025). Code: official repo at commit a4f8433 (2025-08-28, latest). The paper describes memory units as holding the retrieved evidence, but the answer LLM only sees raw evidence at step 0.

sources.code_note: Official repository linked from the paper. Commit a4f8433 (2025-08-28) is the newest; it only has three commits, all from 2025-08-28, so it was released after the first arXiv version (2025-08-14). The repo ships an example on a toy corpus, not the evaluation scripts or configs for the four benchmarks, so the exact settings behind Table 1 cannot be checked.

headline: The answer LLM reads raw text only at step 0. After a failure it reads LLM-written cues (up to 5 'key findings' per layer per probe) and fused notes, never the chunks themselves.
Almost all of the gain comes from the loop: step 0 alone is within 1% of the best baseline on EN.MC (64.6), the full loop reaches 72.93.
The memory pool lives for one question; nothing is carried across questions.

open_questions: The w/o Metacognition ablation removes cues and fusion together; no run keeps cues but drops fusion, so the separate value of Mem-Fuse is unknown.

Because the answer LLM reads cues instead of text after step 0, gains could come from LLM pre-reading (query-focused summarization) as much as from multi-step memory; no baseline gives IRCoT the same summarization.
The loop costs up to 5 cycles of 3 probes × (fact filter + 3 cue calls) per question; the paper reports no per-question tokens or latency for Table 1.

glance.a: A three-part index over the book (chunks in an entity graph, a tree of cluster summaries, window summaries in story order), plus a per-question pool of LLM-written cues.
No. The pool is created for each question and dropped afterwards; only the static index is shared.
Not of chunks. The Veridical path filters the top 5 triples with an LLM before PageRank; the other two layers are plain dense top-k.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: First the raw retrieved text; after a failure, only LLM cues and fused notes.

discussion.takeaway: For questions over whole novels, retrieving once is not enough: letting an LLM probe again after a failed answer, and carrying forward short cues from earlier probes, gives the best scores on four narrative benchmarks with a small retriever.

claims.claim: Best results on all four long-narrative benchmarks.
claims.evidence: EN.MC 72.93 vs 64.19 (HippoRAGv2+IRCoT), EN.QA F1 34.52 vs 34.34 (NV-Embed-v2 RAG), DetectiveQA 68.18 vs 64.77 (RAPTOR+IRCoT). Table 1

claims.claim: The gain comes from the iterative loop, converging in 2-3 cycles.
claims.evidence: Step 0 is within 1% of the best baseline; EN.MC rises from 64.6 to 72.93. Fig. 4, §4.3

claims.claim: The Veridical layer matters most among the indexes.
claims.evidence: Without it EN.MC falls to 51.97 (about -30% relative). Table 2

claims.claim: The loop plugs into other indexes.
claims.evidence: EN.MC 60.26 → 68.56 on HippoRAGv2 and 57.21 → 69.00 on RAPTOR. Table 3
19% relative F1 on EN.QA and 16% accuracy on EN.MC over the strongest baselines for narrative queries. Fig. 6, §4.4

limits: The paper has no limitations section. It notes that the remaining unsolved queries reflect the base LLM's reasoning limits (§4.3).
reading: Baselines and ComoRAG share GPT-4o-mini and BGE-M3 and a 6k context, but ComoRAG makes many more LLM calls per question (probes, cues, fusion, up to 6 answer attempts); cost per question is not reported for Table 1.
In the released code the answer model reads raw text only at step 0; later answers rest on LLM cues, so wrong cues cannot be checked against the source.
Chunks are re-sorted into book order before the token cut, so the kept chunks are the earliest among the top 50 rather than the highest scored; the paper does not mention this.
The query-type analysis (factoid, narrative, inferential) uses the authors' own manual labels (Table 7).
NarrativeQA uses a random 500-question sample and DetectiveQA a random 20% of stories; the samples are not released, so other papers' numbers on these sets are not directly comparable.
The repo has no evaluation scripts or configs for the paper's datasets, so the settings behind Table 1 could not be checked in code.

abstract.text: ComoRAG targets question answering over whole novels, where one-shot retrieval misses how plot and motives change over hundreds of thousands of tokens. It indexes a book three ways (raw chunks linked through an entity graph, recursive cluster summaries, and summaries of consecutive passages). When the model cannot answer, a loop writes new probing queries, turns what each probe finds into short cues in a per-question memory pool, fuses relevant past cues, and tries again. On NarrativeQA, InfiniteBench EN.QA and EN.MC, and DetectiveQA it beats single-step, graph-based and multi-step RAG baselines, with the clearest gains on questions that need the whole storyline.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.
